Calan Martel
About

Materials engineering, close to the bench.

I like being close to the physical problem — running the XRD scan myself, cutting the sample, or machining the fixture so I trust the data it produces. My background spans solid and liquid electrolyte synthesis, battery cell failure analysis, and custom instrumentation design, but the common thread is the same: understand the mechanism first, then build whatever tool the problem actually needs.

I recently completed a Master of Engineering in Materials Science and Engineering at UC Berkeley, where I worked with Lawrence Berkeley National Lab on a solid-state Lithium Lanthanum Zirconium Oxide (LLZO) ceramic electrolyte and led the experimental design for an AI-assisted SEM microstructure study on dual-phase steels. Most recently, I completed a contract at GreenGrid Energy Storage synthesizing a beta-alumina solid electrolyte and building a custom high-temperature test chamber. Before Berkeley, I spent about a year as an R&D engineer at NexTech Batteries working on lithium-sulfur pouch cells, from failure analysis to fixture design.

A few things shape how I work day to day:

When something grabs my interest, I go deep.

First Principles

I want to understand the underlying physics, thermodynamics, and chemistry before I tackle a problem — and I'm not satisfied until I can explain it simply.

Execution Through People

I'm curious about everyone I meet. That's built a wide network, and if I can't solve something myself, I usually know who can.

Cradle to Grave

I like understanding a whole value chain — extraction to recycling — and the business case that makes a technology worth building.

Beyond the Lab

Growing up, I played soccer year-round while ski racing at the international level, and still kept up with school and college applications on top of it. Juggling that much early taught me how to stay focused and work hard — something that's carried straight into how I approach engineering.

Alpine Ski Racing

Two-time California State Champion, and competed at the international level before later coaching at Palisades Tahoe.

Piano

Classically trained pianist — another discipline built on understanding the fundamentals before performance.

Coastal Alaska, from a recent trip.

Projects

Selected Work

Research and engineering projects spanning solid-state ceramics, microstructure characterization, fixture design, and clean-tech commercialization.

Spec — LLZO-2026

Lithium Lanthanum Zirconium Oxide (LLZO) Solid-State Ceramic Electrolyte

With Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, spring 2026. Synthesized an LLZO solid-state ceramic electrolyte as part of a three-person team plus a PhD researcher.

Executed the full ceramic process chain: resin-printed green-body scaffolds on a printer built in-house by the team's PhD researcher, then performed debinding and high-temperature sintering in an argon tube furnace. Analyzed and presented XRD characterization results to the class, visiting PhDs, and course faculty, with data-driven recommendations for next steps.

Spec — Capstone, Master of Engineering

AI-Assisted SEM Microstructure Analysis

Master of Engineering capstone, UC Berkeley, 2025–2026. Leading experimental design for an AI-assisted SEM workflow to characterize microstructure and process-structure relationships in dual-phase steels.

After identifying gaps in existing literature data quality, I proposed and built an in-house data-generation strategy — heat-treating multiple steel grades, cutting and mounting samples, and running a standardized SEM imaging protocol to produce a smaller, higher-quality training dataset for the model.

Spec — DeepTech Commercialization I

Conductive Polymer Binder for Batteries

With Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, advised by Dr. Gao Liu, fall 2025. A four-person team — materials, business, law, and translational medicine — worked to commercialize two polymer binder chemistries developed at LBNL: PFO, which stabilizes high-swelling silicon anodes, and PFM, which revives recycled graphite with a thin conductive coating.

I led patent landscape and competitive analysis, working directly with Haas MBA and Berkeley Law teammates to identify IP gaps (notably weak coverage in China and the EU) and shape go-to-market recommendations. We ran 25 customer discovery interviews out of 110 outreach attempts, talking to teams at Tesla, Toyota, Volkswagen, Redwood Materials, Sila, Coreshell, and BMW i Ventures, and used that input to prioritize the silicon-anode pathway over graphite recycling as the near-term go-to-market.

Patent LandscapeBattery MaterialsCustomer DiscoveryGo-to-Market
Spec — DeepTech Commercialization II

Low-Capital Copper Extraction Strategy

The Red Metal Company, Berkeley DeepTech Commercialization Lab, spring 2026. Partnered biweekly with an early-stage mining-technology founder alongside Haas MBA and Berkeley Law students to shape a low-capital path to commercializing an in-situ copper recovery technology.

Contributed to patent strategy and partnership approach — roughly 80% of the world's copper supply is unreachable through traditional mining, and the project targeted a lower-footprint way to unlock it.

Patent StrategyCleantech MiningGo-to-Market
Spec — Independent Research

"Becoming Literate with AI" — Technical Paper

Summer 2025. I wanted to be able to speak to AI with real understanding rather than just repeating talking points, so I taught myself the field from first principles — starting with the underlying math of how neural networks learn, forward and backpropagation, before working outward from there.

The paper covers the history of AI, neural network architecture, the hardware and infrastructure behind modern models (GPUs, TPUs, cloud compute), the competitive landscape (OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Meta, NVIDIA), and the societal, economic, and ethical implications of AI adoption — written for a general audience. It's part of a broader pattern for me: when something grabs my interest, I go deep, even outside my own field.
